title: Mixed geometric and scalar coherence on strict quotient systems
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and finite extensions $E\subset L\subset M$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ in a fixed algebraic closure, allowing equality, with valuation rings $\mathcal O_F$, uniformizers $\varpi_F$, and $A_{F,n}=\mathcal O_F/\varpi_F^n$ for $n\geq1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. All schemes have $\ell$ invertible [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. On their small pro-etale sites put $R_{F,X}=\lim_n(A_{F,n})_X$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Write $\mathscr S_F(X)$ for the abelian category of strict quotient-module systems with quotient-linear transitions, $\mathcal R_{F,X}$ for derived reduction and $\mathcal L_{F,X}=R\lim\operatorname{Res}$ for realization [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. A system $C$ is normalized when $C_m\otimes^L_{A_{F,m}}A_{F,n}\to C_n$ is an isomorphism for $m\geq n$ [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower].

Use only the finite whole-system operations $U_{f,F}$ and $S_{L/E,X}$ and the comparison maps specified by their adjunction and tensor-generator formulas in [def-trf-integral-comparison-sequence-systems]. For composable scheme maps $Z\xrightarrow hW\xrightarrow kV$, denote the pullback compositor by $c^F_{h,k}:U_{kh,F}\xrightarrow{\sim}U_{h,F}U_{k,F}$, scalar/pullback comparison by $\kappa_f:S_{L/E,X}U_{f,E}\xrightarrow{\sim}U_{f,L}S_{L/E,Y}$, scalar associator by $\alpha_X:S_{M/L,X}S_{L/E,X}\xrightarrow{\sim}S_{M/E,X}$, and scalar multiplication unitor by $e_X:S_{E/E,X}\xrightarrow{\sim}1$. Here $f:X\to Y$ and the respective sources and targets fix all scheme subscripts.

These maps satisfy the following equalities of natural transformations in derived categories of entire quotient diagrams. For $C\in D(\mathscr S_E(V))$,
$$U_{h,L}(\kappa_{k,C})\circ\kappa_{h,U_{k,E}C}\circ S_{L/E,Z}(c^E_{h,k,C})
=c^L_{h,k,S_{L/E,V}C}\circ\kappa_{kh,C}.$$
The $c^F$ are associative and unital for arbitrary composable finite strings of scheme maps, with the canonical inverse-image unit comparisons; equal scheme morphisms give equal comparisons under the canonical identifications. The scalar unit equation is
$$U_{f,E}(e_Y)\circ\kappa_f^{E/E}=e_XU_{f,E}.$$
For $E\subset L\subset M$, the scalar tower equation is
$$U_{f,M}(\alpha_Y)\circ\kappa_f^{M/L}S_{L/E,Y}\circ S_{M/L,X}(\kappa_f^{L/E})
=\kappa_f^{M/E}\circ\alpha_XU_{f,E}.$$
These equalities are induced by equalities on complexes of strict systems, before localization or realization. On flat-term K-flat quotient presentations, the maps are respectively the canonical inverse-image composition map, $1\otimes\gamma_f(x)\mapsto\gamma_f(1\otimes x)$, $c\otimes(b\otimes x)\mapsto cb\otimes x$, and $s\otimes x\mapsto sx$, where $\gamma_f$ is the inverse-image adjunction unit on a local section. The identities include compatibility with every vertical site restriction and every horizontal quotient transition. The assertions hold without normalization, boundedness or finite Tor-amplitude of $C$, and without flatness of the finite coefficient maps; derived scalar maps use simultaneous K-flat models [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings].

source.place: Tag 0D6D, lemma-derived-pullback-composition, termwise K-flat pullback comparison; extracted mixed geometric/coefficient coherence on the ringed sequence site, using the tensor-generator normalization of the blueprint common-stage transport construction.

proof.text: Work in the ringed sequence site of [def-coef-ringed-sequence-site], not in the category of towers in a derived category. Its module sheaves are the strict quotient-semilinear systems in the statement. The geometric maps leave the positive index fixed; scalar change is change of its ring sheaf along the compatible maps $A_{E,n}\to A_{L,n}$. By [def-trf-integral-comparison-sequence-systems], the ordinary comparison maps are the indicated adjunction mates and balanced tensor maps. The adjunct of the geometric compositor on a local section $x$ is the successive unit $\gamma_h\gamma_k(x)$: applying the two adjunction bijections to the mate of fibre-product pasting gives exactly the composite unit. The identity mate gives $\gamma_{\mathrm{id}}(x)=x$ after the unit identification. In the computations below, equality on these unit sections determines a map out of an inverse image by the adjunction bijection; equality on $1\otimes x$ determines a scalar-linear map out of scalar extension by its tensor adjunction. Thus these tests determine the whole sheaf maps, without assuming that arbitrary sections are globally pure tensors.

source.place: Tag 0D6D, lemma-derived-pullback-composition: ordinary composition map; agent expansion using the prescribed sequence-site adjunctions

proof.text: First check geometric coherence on module systems. For three composable scheme maps, either composite of compositors takes the unit section of the composite inverse image to $\gamma_{f_1}\gamma_{f_2}\gamma_{f_3}(x)$. The two underlying fibre-product pastings both send a nested tuple to the same tuple with its three entries, so these are the same section under the canonical base-change identifications. The determining adjunction test of Step 1 proves associativity. Inserting an identity inserts $\gamma_{\mathrm{id}}$, hence leaves this expression unchanged and proves the two unit equations. For an arbitrary finite string, define its comparison by the successively composed units. Induction on the length of a parenthesized string, using the three-map equality at the last junction, identifies every parenthesization with that comparison; the length-zero and length-one cases are the identity units. Equal scheme morphisms induce the same base-change functor and coefficient map; the same adjunction mate therefore gives equal comparisons after these canonical identifications.

source.place: Tag 0D6D, lemma-derived-pullback-composition; agent verification of composition, identity and finite-string coherence

proof.text: For the mixed square use the source generator $1\otimes\gamma_{kh}(x)$ of $S_{L/E,Z}U_{kh,E}C$. The left side first gives $1\otimes\gamma_h\gamma_k(x)$, then $\gamma_h(1\otimes\gamma_k(x))$, then $\gamma_h\gamma_k(1\otimes x)$. The right side gives $\gamma_{kh}(1\otimes x)$ and then $\gamma_h\gamma_k(1\otimes x)$. Here all units carry their prescribed coefficient field, and the constant coefficient sections are identified by the canonical coefficient inverse-image map. The formulas are those of [def-trf-integral-comparison-sequence-systems]. The adjunction and scalar-linearity test of Step 1 therefore proves the displayed mixed geometric equation as an equality of ordinary system maps.

source.place: Tag 0D6D, lemma-derived-pullback-composition; agent calculation of the mixed geometric/scalar square

proof.text: For identity scalar change, start with $1\otimes\gamma_f(x)$. The composite $U_{f,E}(e_Y)\kappa_f^{E/E}$ sends it to $\gamma_f(1x)=\gamma_f(x)$, and $e_XU_{f,E}$ sends it to the same section. For a general coefficient $s$, linearity gives $\gamma_f(sx)=s\gamma_f(x)$ under the constant coefficient identification. The determining test of Step 1 proves the scalar unit equation, including equality fields and the identity scheme map.

source.place: Agent scalar-unit calculation from the tensor formulas prescribed in def-trf-integral-comparison-sequence-systems

proof.text: For the scalar tower equation start with $c\otimes(b\otimes\gamma_f(x))$ in $S_{M/L,X}S_{L/E,X}U_{f,E}C$. On the left the inner $\kappa$ and then the outer $\kappa$ give $\gamma_f(c\otimes(b\otimes x))$; applying $U_{f,M}(\alpha_Y)$ gives $\gamma_f(cb\otimes x)$. On the right $\alpha_XU_{f,E}$ gives $cb\otimes\gamma_f(x)$ and $\kappa_f^{M/E}$ gives $\gamma_f(cb\otimes x)$. Products here use the given inclusion $L\subset M$, exactly as in the associator formula of [def-trf-integral-comparison-sequence-systems]. Balance over $A_{L,n}$ identifies the coefficients $cb$, so this calculation is valid without flatness of any quotient-ring map. Applying the determining test proves the tower equation. It also covers $E=L$, $L=M$, and $E=L=M$.

source.place: Agent scalar-tower calculation from the balanced tensor formulas prescribed in def-trf-integral-comparison-sequence-systems

proof.text: The calculations above are on whole strict systems. To spell out restriction compatibility, let $r$ be a vertical restriction and $q$ a horizontal transition from level $m$ to $n\le m$. Each inverse-image unit is natural, so $r\gamma_f(x)=\gamma_f(rx)$ and $q\gamma_f(x)=\gamma_f(qx)$ under the coefficient restrictions. A scalar tensor restricts as $r(b\otimes x)=r(b)\otimes r(x)$ and transitions as $q(b\otimes x)=q(b)\otimes q(x)$. The quotient coefficient maps are ring homomorphisms, hence $q(cb)=q(c)q(b)$; also $r(cb)=r(c)r(b)$. Consequently restriction of the common answers in Steps 3--5 is respectively $\gamma_h\gamma_k(1\otimes qx)$, $\gamma_f(qs\,qx)$, and $\gamma_f(qc\,qb\otimes qx)$, and applying the comparison after transition gives exactly these answers. Replace $q$ by $r$ for the vertical equations. The geometric formulas in Step 2 commute with $r$ and $q$ by the same unit naturality. Every sequence-site arrow is a composite of vertical and horizontal arrows, so these checks cover every arrow. Termwise application to a complex also commutes with its differential by naturality in the input module; the maps have degree zero and introduce no Koszul sign.

source.place: Agent restriction and quotient-transition verification on the ringed sequence site; Tag 0D6D model comparison

proof.text: For an arbitrary unbounded input choose one flat-term K-flat resolution on its entire ringed sequence site by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. This resolves the strict system as a single ringed-site module complex, rather than choosing unrelated resolutions at each level. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-kflat-pullback], every ordinary geometric pullback and every scalar extension of this complex is again K-flat with flat terms: scalar extension is the special case with identity underlying topos and the actual quotient ring-sheaf map. Repeated application proves the assertion for every intermediate expression in the finite diagrams of Steps 2--5. The sites are the small sequence sites of [def-coef-ringed-sequence-site], and the geometric and coefficient ringed maps are those of [def-trf-integral-comparison-sequence-systems]; thus the cited preservation theorem applies with its actual hypotheses. By [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], the scalar functors and their resolution comparisons are computed on these models and are independent of the chosen K-flat resolution. The geometric functor is exact as specified in [def-trf-integral-comparison-sequence-systems], so its termwise action computes its derived functor. Accordingly the stipulated derived comparison components are precisely the localizations of the cochain maps checked above.

Apply the localization of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] to the equal cochain maps of Steps 2--6 on the simultaneous model of Step 7. A functor takes equal arrows to equal arrows, so all desired equations hold at that model. If $a,b:F\Rightarrow G$ denote the two derived composites of any equation and $p:P\to C$ is the chosen resolution, naturality gives $a_C F(Qp)=G(Qp)a_P$ and $b_C F(Qp)=G(Qp)b_P$. Since $Qp$ is invertible and $a_P=b_P$, cancellation gives $a_C=b_C$. This proves equality for every input and, since the comparisons are natural, equality of natural transformations. Step 6 shows these are equalities localized from the full quotient diagrams before any realization. The resolution and preservation theorems apply to unbounded complexes and arbitrary ring maps. No step used normalization, a bound on cohomology or Tor-amplitude, or flatness of $A_{E,n}\to A_{L,n}$; hence all the stated unrestricted assertions follow.
